messages:
Nia: Quick round-up from the design review of the Routing Policies editor. Found a few UX misunderstandings in the prototype that we should fix before ship. Screenshots in the doc.
Carlos: list them out and we9ll pick sprint-sized fixes.
Nia: TL;DR: 1) Users think list order is decorative; they don9t realize it controls routing priority. 2) The numeric priority field and drag handle convey conflicting affordances. 3) Validation reads too terse: currently says \"invalid\" on priority collisions. 4) Preview simulator truncates differently than runtime, causing false negatives in tests. 5) Keyboard users can9t access the drag handle.
Maya: For #1 propose a small inline label above the list: \"Execution order (top to bottom)\" + tooltip \"Drag to reorder; numbers are for advanced edits.\" That should reduce confusion.
Ethan: Alternate: keep numbers visible but de-emphasize them (muted color) and add a badge on the left that says \"#1\" \"#2\" which matches visual order. That helps users map position to execution.
Nia: I prefer the label approach; less visual noise. Also we should provide a clear affordance for power users to enter \"Edit precedence\" mode where numbers become editable.
Maya: Validation copy needs to be action-oriented. Draft: \"Priority collision \t7 choose a distinct priority or press Auto-resolve to renumber.\" Add a small link \"Auto-resolve\" that runs a deterministic renumber and shows an undo toast.
Carlos: Good. Make sure the undo toast persists long enough and includes a changelist we can inspect.
Ethan: On simulator parity: short-term microcopy under the preview: \"Preview may differ from runtime for very long inputs.\" Long-term: call the runtime preview API or run the same tokenizer. I9ll log an eng dependency.
a11ybot: Accessibility notes: - Make the rule list role=\"list\" and each row role=\"listitem\". - Reorder handle must be keyboard-focusable with aria-roledescription=\"reorder handle\" and provide keyboard moves (Ctrl/Cmd+Up / Down). - Simulator updates should be aria-live=\"polite\" with aria-atomic=\"true\" and the panel should be focus-trap when pinned.
Maya: For keyboard reordering, we can also show a tiny hint on row focus: \"Move: Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down\". People in usability testing noticed the missing affordance.
Nia: Action items: design to produce two comps (default + edit-precedence) with visible focus states and undo toast; copy update for collision + microcopy under preview. Engineering to add keyboard move support and queue tokenizer parity ticket.
Carlos: I'll split this into three tickets and assign priorities. ETA: aim for the UI + copy fixes in the next sprint; tokenizer parity as a follow-up.
Nia: Thanks all. Will upload comps by EOD and schedule a 30-minute review tomorrow at 9:30am.
Ethan: Thanks 44d
Maya: Cheers.
